newsitem.title: UK: Rising staff costs hit UK marketing services firms.
newsitem.headline: Rising staff costs hit UK marketing services firms.

text.p: Britain's marketing services industry is growing at a healthy rate, but companies are being hit by spiralling employment costs, a specialist accountancy firm said on Tuesday.

Willott Kingston Smith said in its "Marketing Monitor" report the fastest growing sectors within the industry were direct marketing, sales promotion and public relations, although it gave no growth figures.
But the accountancy firm said profit per employee was declining in the marketing services industry because employment costs were growing faster than income growth.

"The reason behind the increased levels of staff costs appears to be a reflection of the improving job market and hence a need to retain key people. It has also been exacerbated by the ever increasing cost of recruiting good people to keep up with demand," said the report.
Employment costs represent 52 percent of gross income in direct marketing and sales promotion compared with 51.8 percent in October 1996. The report said this element had hit operating profits.
The accountancy firm compiled "Marketing Monitor" by monitoring eight key performance statistics among leading marketing services companies.
The report said advertising agencies were benefitting from growing advertising expenditures by client companies. But it said ad agencies were a long way away from the boom times of the last decade.
"There is still a long way to go before the levels of the mid 1980s are achieved when the average margin was 10.3 percent," it said.
"Our latest statistics show that 42 percent of the top 50 agencies are currently achieving an operating profit margin of greater than 10 percent," Willott Kingston Smith said.

The report suggests that more agencies should follow the example set by publicly quoted marketing services group, WPP Group Plc, which monitors margins closely and pays performance bonuses based on margins achieved.

The design industry is continuing to recover but is the only sector still earning less income than back in September 1992. Profitability per head has declined. Overall gross income increased by nearly nine percent but increased staff numbers and non-staff operating costs caused a fall in operating profit per head.

"Contrary to popular opinion, our figures do not support the argument that increased employee numbers resulted from taking freelancers onto the payroll as non-staff operating costs increased at an even higher rate," said the report.

Willott Kingston Smith recommends that marketing services companies base staff bonuses and pay raises on performance targets and that they should expand into specialist areas where profit margins are above average.

The firm produces its "Marketing Monitor" by regularly reviewing the latest accounts filed at Companies House by 50 of the UK's largest advertising agencies, 30 direct marketing/sales promotion agencies and 20 of the largest companies in design or media.
